errors.reasoning: updateHumanUserRequestToChangeHuman -> setHumanEmailToEmail renders req.Email.SendCode.UrlTemplate via RenderConfirmURLTemplate; fires if the supplied template string fails to parse.
Same setHumanEmailToEmail template test-render; fires if the parsed template fails to execute against the placeholder data.
ChangeUserHuman calls human.Validate() first, which runs Password.Validate(); thrown if a Password sub-message is set but both Password and HashedPassword are empty.
Password.Validate() calls hasher.ValidateEncodedHash on a supplied HashedPassword; thrown if no configured passwap verifier recognizes the hash's encoding/prefix.
Same ValidateEncodedHash call; thrown when the hash parses but its cost parameters are outside configured bounds.
Same ValidateEncodedHash call; generic fallback for any other hash validation error.
ChangeHuman.Validate() calls Email.Validate() -> EmailAddress.Validate() when Email.Address is non-empty; thrown if net/mail cannot parse the address.
Same EmailAddress.Validate(); thrown if the parsed address includes a display name (e.g. "Name <a@b.c>"), which is rejected.
ChangeHuman.Validate() calls Phone.Validate() -> PhoneNumber.Normalize() when a phone number is set; thrown if libphonenumber cannot parse the given number.
ChangeUserHuman loads the target via UserHumanWriteModel; thrown if the write model shows the user does not exist (deleted or never existed).
ChangeUserHuman calls checkPermissionUpdateUser -> newPermissionCheck whenever human.Changed(); thrown if the aggregateID (userID) passed to the permission check is empty.
Same newPermissionCheck path; thrown if the resource owner cannot be resolved (lookup on the resource-owner model returns none) for the permission check.
checkPermissionUpdateUser's injected permission checker calls authz.CheckPermission -> getUserPermissions; thrown if the request context carries no auth data.
Same getUserPermissions path; thrown when the caller has zero memberships (org- or instance-scoped) to evaluate for user.write.
checkUserResourcePermissions; thrown when the caller's memberships yield no permissions matching user.write, so the update is denied.
Same checkUserResourcePermissions; thrown when the caller has some user.write permissions but none global or scoped to this specific target userID.
When req.Username differs from the current one, changeUsername loads the domain policy; wraps a failure from domainPolicyWriteModel into this precondition-failed error.

changeUsername's call to c.domainPolicyWriteModel throws this internal error if neither an org-level nor an instance-level domain policy write model exists (data inconsistency), which changeUsername then wraps as COMMAND-79pv6e1q62.
changeUsername -> userValidateDomain; thrown if the new username's domain part is a verified org domain belonging to a different org than the user's resource owner.
When req.Password is set, changeUserPassword -> setPasswordCommand checks the (already-existing) user's state; thrown if the user is still in the Initial (not-yet-initialized) state.
When req.Password.CurrentPassword is set, changeUserPassword -> checkCurrentPassword -> verifyPasswordWithLockoutPolicy; thrown if the user's state is Locked.
Same verifyPasswordWithLockoutPolicy call (current-password flow); thrown if the target user has no password hash set yet, so there is nothing to verify against.
Same verifyPasswordWithLockoutPolicy; after the verify attempt it re-checks state and throws this if the user became Locked (e.g. concurrent failed attempts) before this check completed.
checkCurrentPassword's verify closure calls convertPasswapErr on a mismatch between the supplied CurrentPassword and the stored hash; ErrPasswordInvalid wraps that as this error.
Same convertPasswapErr path; thrown if passwap reports the new password is identical to the current one (no-op change).
Same convertPasswapErr; generic internal-error fallback for any other passwap verify/update failure during the current-password check.
When req.Password.VerificationCode is set (no SMS provider configured), changeUserPassword -> setPasswordWithVerifyCode -> verifyCode; thrown if no crypto code was ever generated to verify against.
Same verifyCode; thrown if a code provider ID is present but no external code-verifier resolver was configured.
verifyCode -> crypto.VerifyCode; thrown if the password verification code's expiry has passed.
crypto.VerifyCode -> verifyEncryptedCode; thrown if the stored encrypted code value is nil (no code was ever set).
Same verifyEncryptedCode; thrown if the decrypted stored code does not match the VerificationCode supplied in the request.

When req.Password.Password (plain) is set and the org has no active password complexity policy, checkPasswordComplexity -> getDefaultPasswordComplexityPolicy; thrown if the instance-level default policy write model doesn't exist either.
checkPasswordComplexity -> policy.Check(newPassword); thrown if the new plain password is shorter than the configured MinLength.
Same policy.Check; thrown if the policy requires a lowercase letter and the new password has none.
Same policy.Check; thrown if the policy requires an uppercase letter and the new password has none.
Same policy.Check; thrown if the policy requires a digit and the new password has none.
Same policy.Check; thrown if the policy requires a symbol and the new password has none.
